solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unappealing Disney film about horse delayed the bittersweet stuff

indicators.note: a thing placed about another goes around it, so the film's title is wrapped round the next piece

blocks.note: plain as in not good-looking
Coco is the 2017 Disney-Pixar animated film
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse
delayed means running late

explanation.surface: A grumpy reviewer pans a Disney horse film for coming out late and leaving a bitter taste.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside COCO after its first letter, giving CHOCO; horse for heroin is a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark chocolate without milk is less sweet, so it is described as bittersweet in flavour.

clue.text: Clumsily moving brown fish sandwiches

indicators.note: to sandwich something is to hold it between two outer layers, so the fish surrounds the colour

blocks.note: the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family
umber is an earthy brown pigment

explanation.surface: A clumsy brown fish flops about between slices of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbering describes moving in a heavy, awkward and ungainly way.

clue.text: Rubbish essay's intro penned by popular writer

indicators.note: an intro is the opening part, so only the start of the word essay is used
something penned by another is enclosed in it, as in a pen or fold

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
BS is a vulgar abbreviation for nonsense
the opening letter of essay

explanation.surface: A trashy essay opening is written by a best-selling author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popular' looks like praise for the writer, but it is the word IN, as in fashionable; BS is a vulgar abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: One standing Frank and, occasionally, Bertha up

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter of the name is taken
in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: frank and candid both mean open and honest
the second, fourth and sixth letters of Bertha

explanation.surface: Two people called Frank and Bertha who get up now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate is someone who stands for election, so 'one standing' is a fair description.

clue.text: I see leader of maquis in charge of the Resistance

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its front letter, so only the start of maquis is kept

blocks.note: oh is said when you understand, like I see
first letter of maquis
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Someone realises the head of the maquis commands the French wartime Resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: The maquis were French Resistance fighters, but the capital-R Resistance here is electrical resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ohmic relates to electrical resistance, measured in ohms and named after Georg Ohm.

clue.text: Not even bishop, say, defends OT figure, one without special skills

indicators.note: to defend something is to stand guard around it, so the two outer parts enclose the figure

blocks.note: odd numbers are those that are not even
Job is a figure from the Old Testament
a bishop is an example of a chess man

explanation.surface: An unconventional bishop protects an Old Testament character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not even bishop' reads as an odd bishop, but the oddness and the chessman split apart to hold the biblical figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd-job man does miscellaneous small tasks rather than skilled trade work.

clue.text: Output of a poet in part of cell

blocks.note: the indefinite article, in its form before a vowel
an ode is a lyric poem, the kind of thing produced by the writer that follows
surface padding: names whose output is meant, giving no letters

explanation.surface: Some of a poet's writing was done in a prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as 'an ode', which is what a poet puts out; the cell is an electrical one.
explanation.definitionFit: An anode is the positive electrode of an electrolytic or battery cell.

clue.text: Confusingly catch Anne's trembling hands

indicators.note: trembling letters are shaken up and fall into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
the two hands are right and left, R and L

explanation.surface: Anne's shaking hands fumble a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnarl is to entangle or snare something, catching it in a confusing knot.

clue.text: Son hasn't got any trousers

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to lack something is not to have it

explanation.surface: A boy has no trousers to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Slacks are casual trousers, a plural noun just like the definition.

clue.text: Priests briefly gather on line

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the verb is dropped
one thing written on another sits after it, so the gathering word goes second

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line
to amass is to gather together

explanation.surface: Clergy quickly assemble in a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: The line goes first because the gathering is placed on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamas are Buddhist monks or spiritual teachers in Tibet, so they are priests of a sort.

clue.text: American ponders tailored clothes, and tries to impress

indicators.note: tailored material is cut and remade, so the letters are rearranged
to clothe something is to wrap it up, so the rearranged letters enclose the American

blocks.note: taken as written
Am is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An American thinks about smart suits as a way of showing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailored clothes' looks like a noun phrase about suits, but the words are two separate signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who name-drops mentions famous acquaintances to impress listeners, a verb in the same present tense form.

clue.text: That man interrupts US broadcaster by capital city in Asia

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks into the middle, so the pronoun sits inside the broadcaster

blocks.note: CNN is the American cable news network
he is the pronoun for that man
A1 means first-rate or capital, with the digit 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A man breaks into a US news broadcast from an Asian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like part of 'capital city', but alone it means excellent; Chennai is a state capital in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Chennai, formerly Madras, is a large city in south-east India.

clue.text: Monarch has answer, fixing awkward situation or complaint

indicators.note: to fix something is to fasten it in place, so the monarch and answer hold the situation inside them

blocks.note: CR stands for Carolus Rex, King Charles
A is the abbreviation for answer
to be in a hole is to be in a difficult spot

explanation.surface: A king has the solution that will fix a tricky problem or grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' is the medical sense, an illness, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholera is a serious intestinal disease, and an illness is often called a complaint.

clue.text: Invest in gigantic banking scam

indicators.note: the outer words act as banks on either side, holding the answer between them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of Invest, all of in, and the start of gigantic

explanation.surface: Putting money into a huge banking fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banking' seems to belong with the financial surface, but it is the signal for letters held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A sting is a confidence trick or swindle, the same as a scam.

clue.text: Declining drink, try mixed gin at first

indicators.note: mixed letters are stirred together into a new order
these words say the try and the jumbled spirit come before the drinking word

blocks.note: to have a go is to have a try
taken as written
to down a drink is to swallow it

explanation.surface: Turning down a drink, someone tries a gin cocktail first.
explanation.definitionFit: Going down means falling or decreasing, which is what declining means.

clue.text: Possibly gutsy, I tangled with a bold man

indicators.note: tangled letters are twisted up and come out in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A brave speaker wrestled with a fearless man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutsy' reads as brave, but 'possibly' flags a literal sense: to do with the guts.
explanation.definitionFit: Abdominal means relating to the belly, and 'gutsy' read literally could mean concerning the guts.

clue.text: One could make spirit of policeman calmer

blocks.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
stiller means more still, so calmer

explanation.surface: A calming officer can raise people's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests morale, but here it is alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A distiller produces spirits such as whisky or gin by distillation.

clue.text: What jewellery thief did without diamonds, laughing softly

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the card-suit letter is taken out

blocks.note: a thief nicked, or stole, a ring
D is the abbreviation for the card suit diamonds

explanation.surface: A jewel thief who skipped the diamonds and chuckled quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick is British slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickering is the soft whinny of a horse, and by extension a quiet snigger or chuckle.

clue.text: World traveller aboard English ship — this may prevent sight-seeing

blocks.note: Phileas Fogg went Around the World in Eighty Days
aboard means in
E is the abbreviation for English
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A globetrotter on an English ship finds the view spoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Fogginess is mistiness, which blocks the view and so could stop tourists seeing the sights.

clue.text: Bacon, perhaps, I stuffed in some European bread

indicators.note: something stuffed in is packed into the middle of something else

blocks.note: bread is slang for money, and francs were the currency of France, Belgium and others
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs bacon into a European loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bacon' reads as meat, but the capital B marks a person, and 'bread' means money.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was both an Elizabethan philosopher and a twentieth-century painter, so Bacon is an example.

clue.text: Tin backing on decorative material

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the letters run from right to left

blocks.note: a tin is a can
re means on or about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Tin is used to support some ornamental fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre is mother-of-pearl, the iridescent shell lining used in inlay and ornament.

clue.text: Part of the fare of Parisian in plane, say

blocks.note: en is French for in
the plane is a kind of tree, common in Paris streets

explanation.surface: A Parisian's airline ticket price, travelling in a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' and 'plane' suggest air travel; fare is food and the plane is a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: An entree is a course of a meal, and a meal's food is its fare.

clue.text: Adult books one summer period around tropical island

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the month's letters run backwards

blocks.note: A is the film certificate for adult
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
I is the Roman numeral for one
Aug is the abbreviation for August, a summer month

explanation.surface: A grown-up reserves a summer holiday on a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Books' looks like a verb (reserves), but it is a noun for a part of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is a Caribbean island, part of the nation of Antigua and Barbuda.

clue.text: Where Riviera tourists go, wanting stimulant boost

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the drug's letter is taken away

blocks.note: tourists on the French Riviera head to Nice
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Riviera holidaymakers who need a pick-me-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is something that invigorates or lifts the spirits, a boost.

clue.text: A Greek princess accepts kiss, and maiden accepted proposition

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the kiss goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
X is the mark for a kiss
Io was a princess of Argos in Greek myth, loved by Zeus
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A Greek princess lets a man kiss her, and the young woman accepts his proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: The kiss sits between A and IO, which together form the container. 'Proposition' looks like a marriage offer but means a statement.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a statement taken as true without proof, an accepted proposition.

clue.text: Check nose of plane? Perhaps fly around

indicators.note: the nose is the front, so only the first letter of plane is taken
a thing around another encloses it

blocks.note: a fly is an example of an insect
the opening letter of plane

explanation.surface: Examine the front of an aircraft, or perhaps take it up and circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like a verb about piloting the plane, but it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine closely, which is to check.

clue.text: It indicates resignation of personnel, you heard, in case of sexting

indicators.note: heard says the word is taken by its sound, giving a letter that sounds the same
something in a case is enclosed, and the case of a word is its outer pair of letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of sexting
HR, human resources, is the personnel department
the letter U sounds like you

explanation.surface: A staff member quits after a sexting scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resignation' looks like quitting a job, but here it means acceptance of the inevitable.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrug of the shoulders is the classic gesture of resigned acceptance.

clue.text: Criminal in clear, so working to clean things up

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or bent, so the letters are twisted out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crook is cleared and goes straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like the subject of the sentence; it is the signal for rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Censorial means relating to a censor, whose task is purging offensive material.

clue.text: Mother caught some sunshine

indicators.note: caught here means picked up by ear, so the word is used for its sound

blocks.note: rays of the sun

explanation.surface: Mum got a bit of a tan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb to look after.
explanation.definitionFit: To mother a child is to bring it up, which is to raise it.

clue.text: A liability for the House? Rees-Mogg can't do otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters are set out differently

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Jacob Rees-Mogg, a Conservative MP, is an embarrassment to the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The House' suggests Parliament, but it is a home; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A second mortgage is an additional loan secured on a home, a debt on the house.
